objectives.text: Purpose of the AML/CFT subchapter: to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing through the establishment by financial institutions of reasonably designed, risk-based programs to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism.

citations.quote: prevent the laundering of money and the financing of terrorism through the establishment by financial institutions of reasonably designed risk-based programs to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism;

objectives.text: Purpose of AMLA 2020 to reinforce that AML/CFT policies, procedures, and controls of financial institutions must be risk-based.

citations.quote: to reinforce that the anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policies, procedures, and controls of financial institutions shall be risk-based;

obligations.actor: Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator
obligations.action: take into account specified statutory factors when prescribing minimum AML/CFT program standards and when supervising and examining institutions for compliance with those standards
obligations.trigger: prescribing minimum standards under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(2)(A) and supervising/examining compliance with those standards

citations.quote: In prescribing the minimum standards under subparagraph (A), and in supervising and examining compliance with those standards, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the appropriate Federal functional regulator (as defined in section 509 of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (12 U.S.C. 6809)) shall take into account the following:

obligations.actor: anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism programs described in 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1) (i.e., financial institutions' programs)
obligations.action: be reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of the subchapter and its regulations, and be risk-based, directing more attention and resources toward higher-risk customers and activities rather than lower-risk customers and activities, consistent with the institution's risk profile

citations.quote: reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the requirements of this subchapter and regulations promulgated under this subchapter

risk-based, including ensuring that more attention and resources of financial institutions should be directed toward higher-risk customers and activities, consistent with the risk profile of a financial institution, rather than toward lower-risk customers and activities.

obligations.action: establish and make public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators, relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies
obligations.trigger: not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(4)

citations.quote: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this paragraph, the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators
shall establish and make public priorities for anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policy.

obligations.action: update the AML/CFT priorities established under subparagraph (A), in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators, relevant State financial regulators, and relevant national security agencies
obligations.trigger: not less frequently than once every 4 years

citations.quote: Not less frequently than once every 4 years, the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Attorney General, Federal functional regulators
shall update the priorities established under subparagraph (A).

obligations.action: review the priorities established by the Secretary and incorporate those priorities, as appropriate, into the institution's risk-based AML/CFT programs established to meet obligations under the subchapter, the USA PATRIOT Act, and other AML/CFT laws and regulations; that review and incorporation is then used as a supervisory/examination measure
obligations.trigger: existence of published national AML/CFT priorities under subparagraph (A)

citations.quote: The review by a financial institution of the priorities established under subparagraph (A) and the incorporation of those priorities, as appropriate, into the risk-based programs established by the financial institution to meet obligations under this subchapter
shall be included as a measure on which a financial institution is supervised and examined for compliance with those obligations.

obligations.actor: persons in the United States responsible for a financial institution's AML/CFT program
obligations.action: remain responsible for, and personally perform, the duty to establish, maintain, and enforce the institution's anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism program, while being accessible to and subject to oversight and supervision by the Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator
obligations.trigger: duty to establish, maintain and enforce an AML/CFT program as required under 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)

citations.quote: The duty to establish, maintain and enforce an anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism program as required by this subsection shall remain the responsibility of, and be performed by, persons in the United States
who are accessible to, and subject to oversight and supervision by, the Secretary of the Treasury and the appropriate Federal functional regulator

notes: This source item is Division F of the AML Act of 2020 as an uncodified/note-level compilation; most operative program-establishment text (the substance of 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(1)-(2)) is amended by cross-reference/insertion rather than reproduced in full, so several core program obligations (e.g., the base duty to establish an AML program) are only partially visible in this source and are extracted as given, without filling gaps from the main codified text (out of scope for this item). Per the fidelity rule, ambiguity as to full program content is preserved rather than resolved. Boundary/coordination-layer content (SAR/CTR specifics, OFAC/sanctions, whistleblower provisions, beneficial ownership/CTA reporting details, GAO studies, personnel/administrative provisions) is described only where it bears directly on program-establishment obligations; most of Titles LXI-LXV is administrative, reporting, or study-related and outside the ratified program-rules scope, so it was not extracted as obligations.
